conditions: g differentiable at x and f differentiable at g(x).
spoken_aliases: the derivative with respect to x of f composed with g evaluated at x equals f prime evaluated at g of x times g prime evaluated at x
d by d x of f of open parenthesis g of x close parenthesis equals f prime of open parenthesis g of x close parenthesis times g prime of x

evidence: Write the increment of g as g'(x)h+o(h). Differentiability of f at g(x) gives the increment of f as f'(g(x)) times the increment of g plus a remainder little-o of that increment. Since the increment of g is O(h), the total increment is f'(g(x))g'(x)h+o(h). This argument also covers vanishing increments.
